summary: You need 45 graduate units, at least 36 of them letter graded, and no more than 10 units of Foundations courses count toward the 45. Foundations are CS 103, CS 109 (or CS 221 or 229 plus a probability course), CS 161, CS 107 and CS 111; a course waived for work done elsewhere is marked by hand. Breadth takes three courses from three different areas, and every breadth and depth course must be letter graded and 3 or more units; your subplan's depth needs 21 units, with at most 6 units of CS 399. One course with a significant software implementation is required and may also count elsewhere. Electives, which only fill out the 45 units, are any CS course above 111 taken for 3 or more units, except CS 161A, 196, 198 and 390A-C; other technical courses and School of Engineering seminars need approval and are moved in by hand. You check by hand the 3.0 GPA on the graded units and, for distinction in research, the research experience, GPA and report.
